roadmap.goal: A breach of the frontend or backend time budget fails the build on plain CI runs, limits are measured on plain runs, an allow-list entry that is not needed fails the check, and the warn-only switch is read by the check itself from LIGHTHOUSE_BUDGET_WARN_ONLY.
roadmap.notes: Slice 3 (docs close-out: ci-learnings.md, ADR-237 amendment, ADR-268 status line, brief, feature-delta wrap-up) is deliberately NOT in this roadmap: docs wait for the maintainer's confirmation per the project rule. The after-push read (at least 5 green main runs on both budget steps) is elapsed-time work and is not a step either. 25 tests in the test file are skipped; each belongs to exactly one step below (01-01: 9, 01-02: 10, 02-01: 5, 02-02: 1). Nothing is pushed.

phases.name: S1 The check owns the switch and knows what is not needed
phases.description: check_budget.py reads LIGHTHOUSE_BUDGET_WARN_ONLY itself and judges allow-list entries that are not needed; the shipped limits are untouched.

steps.name: The budget check reads its warn-only switch from the environment
steps.description: Replace the stub of warn_only_requested and wire it into the check. Unset, empty or false enforces; the exact lowercase value true turns a breach into a warning and prints a notice naming the variable and saying enforcement is off; the flag wins over the variable whatever its value; any other value gives no verdict (exit 2) and names the variable, even when nothing is over budget.
criteria: An unset, empty or false variable enforces: a breach on either stack fails with the phrase took 70.0s, over the 60s budget
The variable set to true turns a breach on either stack into a warning with the same phrase and exit 0, and a notice line names the variable and says enforcement is off
No notice is printed while the budget is enforced
--warn-only warns whatever the variable says, including maybe and TRUE
TRUE, True, 1, yes, on, a value with surrounding spaces and maybe give no verdict, exit 2, with an error naming the variable; this also holds when nothing is over the budget
With the variable true, a breach is a warning while a stale entry in the same run still fails with exit 1, and no error line names the breached unit
Missing timing file and malformed allow-list still give no verdict under true (unchanged)
The existing 85 tests in test_check_budget.py stay green and unedited
Comments follow the project rule: no internal references, no nWave scenario tags
steps.implementation_notes: Remove the unittest.skip decorators of the 9 listed tests and make them pass; run them red first. Contract is pinned in the Pre-requisites of feature-delta.md: values matched exactly, no trimming, case-sensitive; the notice is a ::notice:: annotation; an invalid value is an ::error:: and exit 2. Keep the pure function separate from the shell. Commit: feat(test-infra): the budget check reads its warn-only switch itself.

steps.name: An allow-list entry that is not needed fails the check
steps.description: Replace the stub of unneeded_entries with both rules (a ceiling equal to the budget on either stack; on the frontend, an entry above the budget whose file ran under a quarter of the budget) and add the failure annotation. The check wires only the static rule here: it passes no run rows, so the frontend run-time rule stays off until step 02-01. The shipped file is held to the same rule.
criteria: An entry whose ceiling equals the budget fails on both stacks, naming the unit, the allow-list file and the words not needed, exit 1
The same failure holds when the variable is true and when --warn-only is given, like a stale entry
A ceiling below the budget is never named, and a ceiling above the budget passes: only a ceiling equal to the budget is named, on both stacks
A frontend file that ran under a quarter of the budget is named and one at exactly a quarter is not; a frontend entry below the budget is never named for running little
A backend class is never named for running little; an entry missing from the run is left to the stale check; nothing is named when every entry is needed
With no run rows only ceilings are judged, and the shipped budget file holds no entry the check would call not needed on either stack
This step passes no run rows to the check, so a frontend file that ran quickly is not yet judged on a real run
Comments follow the project rule: no internal references, no nWave scenario tags
steps.implementation_notes: Remove the unittest.skip decorators of the 10 listed tests. Test 18 (a frontend entry whose file ran under a quarter of the budget, run through the CLI) is NOT in this step: it needs the run's rows and belongs to 02-01. The function judges the run-time rule when rows are given; the check wires it with an empty row list here. Commit: feat(test-infra): a budget allow-list entry that is not needed fails the check.

phases.name: S2 Measured limits, then enforcement
phases.description: The budget file holds limits measured on plain CI runs, the frontend run-time check goes on, and both workflows enforce the budget.

steps.name: Limits measured on plain runs, and the frontend run-time check on
steps.description: New test-time-budget.json: frontend budget 56 s with an empty list; backend budget 34 s with the 23 entries of the tighten-only variant (16 tightened, 3 unchanged, 4 new). The check now passes the run's rows, so the frontend run-time not-needed check is on. Replay the new file over every frontend and backend timing CSV of the measurement and plant a slow unit on each stack.
criteria: The shipped frontend budget is 56 s and nothing is allow-listed
The shipped backend budget is 34 s and the list is exactly the 23 measured ceilings, none raised above its previous value except the four named new classes
A frontend file entry above the budget whose file ran 13.9 s against a budget of 56 fails naming the entry and not needed, exit 1
A planted frontend file of 57 s fails the build against the shipped file with the phrase took 57.0s, over the 56s budget
A planted backend class of 35 s only warns with exit 0 when the variable is true
Replay of the shipped file over all 7 frontend and 8 backend timing CSVs of the measurement exits 0 on every one, and the command is recorded in feature-delta.md
The shipped file holds no entry the check would call not needed, and every backend entry still names a class in the test source
Comments follow the project rule: no internal references, no nWave scenario tags
steps.implementation_notes: Remove the unittest.skip decorators of the 5 listed tests. The ceilings are fixed by D-6462-15 (tighten-only) and by the SHIPPED_BACKEND_CEILINGS table in the test file; do not re-derive or raise a limit without a decision (D-6462-22). Order 02-01 before 02-02 matters: the step must never enforce limits measured on coverage runs. The replay is the local proof that the first push does not turn red. Commit: fix(test-infra): set the time budgets from plain CI runs.

steps.name: Both workflows enforce the budget in a step of its own
steps.description: In ci_backend.yml and ci_frontend.yml split the unit-test run into a step Test the budget check (no switch in its env) and keep Check test-time budget with the switch in its env, read through LIGHTHOUSE_BUDGET_WARN_ONLY. The backend loses --warn-only; the frontend loses its case block and the BUDGET_WARN_ONLY env and its --warn-only branch; comments are rewritten.
criteria: On both stacks the unit-test step runs the unit suite only and does not run check_budget.py, does not carry the switch and does not carry --warn-only
On both stacks the Check test-time budget step carries the switch in its env, read from the repository variable LIGHTHOUSE_BUDGET_WARN_ONLY, and does not carry --warn-only
The frontend workflow has no case block and no BUDGET_WARN_ONLY env
The backend budget step no longer runs with --warn-only, so a breach fails the build
actionlint reports nothing on the changed workflows; the comments above the steps say what they do in plain language, with no internal references and no nWave scenario tags
The full test-timings unit suite is green
steps.implementation_notes: Remove the unittest.skip decorator of the one listed test. The unit-test step runs python3 -m unittest discover -s Scripts/test-timings/tests as today, but apart from the budget step. Nothing is pushed; the push waits for the maintainer. Commit: ci(test-infra): the backend time budget fails the build.
